collaredlemming: A scientific field-guide illustration of a collared lemming in winter, STRICT SIDE PROFILE, standing on all four feet on the ground. Natural wild proportions: a compact vole-shaped body about as long as a human thumb, a low back, short legs, and a blunt head continuous with the shoulders. SMALL DARK EYES SET FLAT IN THE FUR, no larger in proportion than a real rodent's. Dense white winter fur hides the ears. On each front foot the two middle claws are thick, pale and forked.
bumblebeebat: A scientific field-guide illustration of a bumblebee bat in STRICT SIDE PROFILE, hanging upright on a vertical surface with its wings folded closed along its flanks. Natural wild proportions: a slender body no longer than a thumb joint, a narrow chest, long thin forearms folded tight. SMALL BLACK EYES, correctly tiny for a bat. Short truncated muzzle with a swollen fleshy nose-pad, large upright ears, fine reddish-brown fur, dark leathery wing membrane.
kangaroorat: A scientific field-guide illustration of a kangaroo rat in STRICT SIDE PROFILE standing on both hind feet. Natural wild proportions: a lean sandy-buff rodent with a small narrow head, LONG NARROW HIND FEET as long as its own shin, powerful thighs, and tiny forelimbs held close. SMALL DARK EYES set flat in the face, correctly proportioned for a rodent. Its tail is longer than head and body together, thin and bare with a small flat tuft at the tip.
remora: A scientific field-guide illustration of a remora in STRICT SIDE PROFILE. Natural proportions: a slim streamlined dark grey fish. On the top of its head lies a FLAT OVAL SUCKING DISC that is FLUSH WITH THE SKULL AND NO WIDER THAN THE HEAD ITSELF, reaching from the snout to just behind the eyes and NO FURTHER - a shallow ridged plate, never raised above the head, never overhanging the body, never larger than the head. Lower jaw juts forward, small forked tail.
portuguesemanowar: A scientific illustration of a Portuguese man o' war viewed FROM THE SIDE AT THE WATERLINE. Its float is a LONG NARROW HORIZONTAL BLADDER lying flat like a slender pointed pod, several times longer than it is tall, tapering to a point at each end - it has NO DOME, NO BELL and NO ROUNDED CAP. A thin ruffled crest runs along the top ridge. Translucent pale blue and rose. Fine bright blue tentacles of unequal length trail from beneath one end.
hoodedseal: A scientific field-guide illustration of a hooded seal in STRICT SIDE PROFILE lying flat. Natural proportions: a heavy silver-grey seal blotched with black, its head small relative to its thick body. From ONE NOSTRIL at the very front of the muzzle protrudes a smooth red sac of nasal lining, HANGING FORWARD AND DOWNWARD FROM THE TIP OF THE NOSE AND NO LARGER THAN THE SEAL'S OWN SNOUT. Its eye is small, dark and set flat in the face.
